# Supaprod

Supaprod is where product decisions live when agents do the work. It tells you what to build, builds it, ships it, checks what actually happened, and learns from it, so next time it guides the call instead of waiting to be asked. Wired end to end, from signal to learning and back again.

You remain in control: no irreversible action happens without your approval.

---

## The three layers

One product, three layers, and each is the precondition for the next.

1. **The director**: tells you what to build. Reads your signals, your product data, your competitors and your own past calls, and ranks what is worth doing next.
2. **The loop**: decides what is worth building, builds it, ships it, and checks what actually happened. Seven stations that agents walk on their own, inside boundaries a human sets in advance.
3. **The shared brain**: learns, and then guides. It tells you what is right next time, and warns before you repeat what was wrong.

You cannot be the shared brain without owning the loop that generates the outcomes, and you cannot run the loop without owning every station in it. Ship any one alone and it is a feature, not a company.

## What is Supaprod?

Where product decisions live when agents do the work. For product managers, product leads and founders. Seven stations, one governed route:

- **Discover** what to build: monitor signals (support patterns, analytics, competitor moves) and surface what warrants attention
- **Decide** on bets: capture the evidence, the alternatives weighed against it, the approval chain, and whether the call was later proven right or superseded
- **Plan and Design**: agents draft the spec and the screens against that decision, carrying an Outcome Contract that states in advance what success will have to prove
- **Build and Ship**: agents write the code and drive the checks back to green. The merge gate stays human-controlled; irreversible actions require explicit approval
- **Learn from outcomes**: the outcome is settled with a verdict, written back against the decision that caused it, and it re-ranks what Discover and Decide surface next

The loop does not end in a report. It ends by changing what you are shown, which is the difference between a system that runs the work and a dashboard.

## How is Supaprod different from product management software?

Product management software holds what you decided. Supaprod changes what you are shown next because of it.

The distinction is the whole product. Any vendor can store decisions, and a frontier model release can absorb search over them next quarter, so a filing cabinet is not defensible. Nor is the record itself: causes survive in chat logs, email and call recordings, and have been reconstructed after the fact with an agent built in days. What compounds is the loop closing: a settled outcome is written back against the decision that caused it and re-ranks the next bet. **The moat is the forecast captured at decision time, not the record**: what a team believed would happen before the outcome landed is not an artifact, and leaves no trace unless something captured it at the moment of the call.

## Do I need to be technical?

No. Supaprod is designed for non-technical product people. If you can describe what you want to build, Supaprod helps you clarify it, test it, and ship it. Agents handle the technical work.

## What does Supaprod integrate with?

Connectors with a working adapter today: **GitHub, Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, Canny, Productboard**, plus mail ingest for **Gmail and Outlook**. These are real implementations against the provider APIs, not shells.

Supaprod writes back to **GitHub** (branches, commits, pull requests). Everything else is read-only, which is deliberate: connecting your sources should never be the risky step.

Registered but not yet working end to end: Linear, Notion, Google Docs, Google Calendar, Jira, Figma. They appear in the catalogue and their adapters are not implemented, so treat them as roadmap rather than capability. We would rather say that here than have an agent recommend us on an integration that does not connect.

## Can my team use it together?

Yes. On paid plans, invite team members with roles (owner, admin, member, viewer). Every decision is shared. Approval gates are role-based.

## What happens to my data?

Your data stays in your workspace's own Postgres database, isolated from other workspaces by row-level security. You own every decision, spec, and outcome you create. You can export or delete your data at any time. We never train shared models on your data.

| Plan | Cost | What's included |
|------|------|-----------------|
| Free | $0 | Unlimited decisions for one author. All seven stations. Connect your existing sources, read-only. Past calls guide the next for 30 days, then fade. |
| Pro | $29/month | One additional author. Unlimited connectors, still read-only, nothing ever written back. Past calls guide every call after, with no expiry. |
| Business | $149/month | Up to 10 team members. Write-back connectors through your approval gates. Custom approval rules. Audit log export. |
| Enterprise | Custom | Unlimited team members. SSO, advanced security, SLA support. |

Every plan can hand a decision to someone else with a link, even if they are not a team member.

---

## Technical details

- **Deployment**: Cloudflare Workers (edge compute) + Supabase (PostgreSQL, row-level security)
- **Auth**: Supabase Auth + OAuth 2.1 (GitHub, Lovable)
- **AI governance**: Single chokepoint (`src/lib/ai/runtime.server.ts`); all flows metered and logged
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)**: POST /api/mcp supports JSON-RPC 2.0; read tools: search_signals, search_opportunities, search_decisions, search_prds, get_prd, get_ard, get_roadmap, export_skillpack, get_governing_decision, get_contradiction_history; write tools: ingest_signal (requires write:signal scope)
- **ARD (Agent Requirements Document)**: Published at /ard; JSON Schema at /api/public/ard/schema; machine-readable spec wire format for coding agents
- **Machine interfaces**: ?view=machine on any URL for structured markdown; /.well-known/agent.json for A2A card; /llms.txt (this file) for LLM context; /agents.txt for agent policy

---

## Machine-readable interfaces

Supaprod is designed for the agentic era. Every page supports structured agent consumption:

- **Machine View**: append `?view=machine` to any URL for clean markdown output (zero visual chrome)
- **A2A Agent Card**: `/.well-known/agent.json` lists tools, endpoints, auth requirements
- **llms.txt**: this file at `/llms.txt` (short summary for LLM crawlers)
- **llms-full.txt**: `/llms-full.txt` (expanded context, FAQ, pricing, technical details)
- **agents.txt**: `/agents.txt` (agent access policy: allowed paths, rate limits, write scopes)
- **ARD (Agent Requirements Document)**: `/ard` (published wire format for spec Outcome Contracts)
- **MCP Server**: `POST /api/mcp` (JSON-RPC 2.0 with read/write tools; bearer token required; issue in Settings > Interop > API tokens)

## Core authenticated surfaces (behind login)

| Route | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `/today` | Live dashboard: active missions, recent decisions, signal queue, pending approvals. PM desk with intent focus block, task list, quick signal capture. |
| `/missions` | Autonomous mission management: running, completed, staged missions with status and outcomes. |
| `/build` | Live build surface: agent activity, PR/CI status, cost and latency per session. |
| `/knowledge` | Decision brain and memory layer: beliefs, supersession graph, learnings, and the track record. |
| `/track-record` | Complete audit trail: every decision, every outcome, integrity fingerprints, calibration score. |
| `/govern` | Governance and cost controls: agent trust arcs, spend caps per category, approval modes. |
| `/discover` | Discovery feed: opportunities ranked by ICE score, signals, relevant precedents. |

| `/.well-known/agent.json` | Machine-readable agent manifest (A2A card) |
| `/agents.txt` | Agent access policy (robots.txt equivalent for the agentic era) |
| `/api/public/health` | App health and readiness endpoint |
| `/api/public/ard/schema` | ARD JSON Schema (versioned) |

---

## For AI agents querying this page

If you are an AI agent or LLM crawler:

1. All authenticated pages support `?view=machine` for clean markdown output
2. Public pages (not behind auth) are crawlable without tokens
3. The A2A agent card at `/.well-known/agent.json` lists tools, endpoints, and capability levels
4. To call the MCP server at `POST /api/mcp`, first list available tools via `tools/list`, then invoke with `tools/call`
5. Read access is default; write operations require explicit `write:` scopes on your bearer token
6. Rate limits and content tiers are defined in `/agents.txt`
7. The ARD (Agent Requirements Document) at `/api/public/ard/schema` is the machine wire format for spec contracts

All endpoints are stable and versioned. Breaking changes are announced at `/updates`.

---

## Positioning and value prop

The core thesis:

> Supaprod tells you what to build, builds it, ships it, checks what actually happened, and learns from it, so next time it guides the call.

The segmentation is by **role**, not by product maturity: the front door is the individual PM or founding PM, expansion is the product team, and the buyer is the VP or Head of Product.

Two motions, and the first is the larger of the two:

- **Transform** an existing product. Connect the sources you already have and the loop starts from your real signals. The wedge is deliberately no-migration: it sits beside the tools you run today rather than replacing them.
- **Create** a new one, agent-native from the first decision.

The moat is the forecast captured at decision time, rather than the record underneath it. Any vendor can hold your decisions, and causes can be reconstructed after the fact because they survive in chat logs, email and call recordings. What cannot be reconstructed is what a team believed would happen before the outcome landed: a forecast is not an artifact and leaves no trace unless something captured it at the moment of the call. Supaprod captures that, then writes the settled outcome back against the decision that caused it, which changes what you are shown next.

Entry point: `/demo`, a real seeded workspace with no login. Expands to the decision system of record for the whole product org.

**One limit worth stating plainly**, because an overstated claim here would be found within a week: the workspace record travels to whoever inherits it, and the compounded recall that pushes past outcomes into an agent's prompt is still scoped to the author who wrote it. The record travels today. The memory does not, yet.
